svg.text: RP2040-Plus + BTT TMC5160T Plus Y concept review
REVIEW ONLY: not active printer wiring. Bench-validate before construction.
Pico: STEP=GPIO0, DIR=GPIO1, ENABLE=GPIO2, DIAG1=GPIO3, endstop=GPIO4,
TMC1_J1/J2/TOP model the ordinary StepStick-format adapter and supplied ribbon as one boundary.
Continuity-check the received adapter/ribbon and mark pin 1 before applying power.
TMC1 J1: EN, MOSI/CFG1, SCK/CFG2, CS/CFG3, MISO/CFG0, CLK N/C, STEP, DIR.
TMC1 J2: regulated auxiliary 24V, two grounds, B2/B1/A1/A2 N/C, sequenced VIO.
TMC1 TOP: DIAG0 is electrically unused and DIAG1 is the protected GPIO3 return;
both are physical through-pins and require carrier holes.
U1 is SN7407N DIP-14. U2 is ILD74 DIP-8. Both use the shown top-view pin numbering.
U3 is the received UTC LP2950L-3.3 in TO-92. Its pinout is pin 1=OUT,
pin 2=GND, pin 3=IN. Follow the flat-face orientation in the top component
view and verify those three functions before insertion.
A/B/C/HV are AR20-HZW/TN 20-pin, 0.3-inch DIL wire-wrap sockets with spring contacts.
Physical layout: Pico at the left; Socket A above U1; the HV socket above Socket C;
the TMC adapter and 18-pin external I/O row precede the full driver footprint.
Top-row parts align with the Pico USB edge. Keep that area clear except for the plate's USB bridge.
Insert each passive across its labeled opposite contact pair; the passive itself joins the pair.
Socket HV contacts 1-4 and 20-17 hold U2 pins 1-4 and 8-5.
Positions 6-8 and 15-13 hold R1A/R1B/R1C; positions 9-10 hold DZ1/D1.
HV positions 5 and 16 remain empty as a physical guard row between U2 and
the detector passives. Do not use those contacts for low-voltage circuitry.
Socket A keeps the earlier placement: positions 1-4 hold C1/C2/R2/R3,
position 6 holds R5, and position 7 holds C3 in place of the old DZ2.
The removed R4's A05/A16 contacts remain the U3 input/output feed points.
A08/A09/A10 hold Q1 C/B/E on one side.
A13/A12/A11 hold U3 pins 1/2/3 (OUT/GND/IN) on the opposite side.
Verify the actual BC327 lead order before inserting Q1.
Socket B positions 2-8 hold R6, R12, R7, R11, R8, R10, R9 in that order;
Socket C positions 1-10: R15, R18, R17, R16, R19, R20, R13, R14, R21, R22.
HV optocoupler labels use U2P=ILD74 pin, LEDA/LEDB=channel, A/K=anode/cathode,
DZ1 contacts marked K/A are cathode/anode. D1 K goes to U2 pin 1; D1 A to U2 pin 3.
C2=C3=100nF ceramic. C3 replaces the old DZ2 without moving its leads.
PWR_OK_N is active-low: LOW means fused MOTOR_HVIN is valid; it is a reporting input only.
Wire colors: red=positive power; black=ground; blue=STEP/SCLK; yellow=all other signals;
grey on the drawing=physical white wire for Pico 3.3V and sequenced VIO.
U1 collectors are pulled up only from sequenced TMC_VIO. U3 is fed from
Pico USB VBUS only after Q1 is enabled by the HVIN detector.
Logic, detector, and VIO conductors are low-current wire-wrap class only.
The external I/O row carries both external 5A fuse contacts, MOTOR_HVIN through two
paralleled positive contacts, regulated auxiliary 24V through two paralleled contacts,
and two paralleled ground contacts. Connect the serviceable external fuse only between
MOTOR_HVIN may be 24V to 48V; AUX_24V must remain regulated 24V maximum.
When both domains are 24V, bridge them only in the external harness, not on this board.
Its carrier uses a separately printed bottom upholder; the long wire-wrap tails point down.
Keep LINE18_NC_ISOLATION and LINE18_SPARE_03 through LINE18_SPARE_08 unconnected.
High-current MOTOR_HVIN bypasses the Pico and DIL-socket conductors.
Land the four Y-motor conductors directly on the driver's 1B/2B/1A/2A screw terminals.
The 64x57mm driver box is exact; screw-terminal spacing within it is illustrative.
F1 is a dedicated serviceable external 5A branch fuse.
Size and insulate all high-current wiring for the fuse rating and 48V maximum.

g.text: Follow the labels at both ends of every highlighted edge.
Dashed edges are old wraps to pull out; do not re-wrap them.
